subject: Urgent: Hosted API throughput regression — queue depth and batching causing p99 spike
messages:
From: Emma Carter <emma@clarityhealth.com>

Date: 2027-01-30T08:02:00Z
Subject: Production: sudden p99 jumps and 5xxs this morning

Hi Grace / Dylan —

We're seeing a sustained rise in p95/p99 across our Hosted API traffic starting ~07:30 PT. P95 previously ~320ms is now ~1.4s and p99 is spiking above 4s; error rate elevated to ~0.9%. Throughput looks similar to normal. This is affecting latency-sensitive workflows for several doctors in our pilot.

We've attached a couple of request samples and a small screenshot of the p99 trend. Can your team triage and share ETA?

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-30T09:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Production: sudden p99 jumps and 5xxs this morning

Logging my initial findings from the cluster that hosts ClarityHealth's tenant:

- Observed queue_depth for their routing shard increased from baseline ~2.1k to a sustained ~18k between 07:25–08:40 PT.
- Batch formation latency jumped: average time-to-fill batch rose from ~12ms to ~460ms due to queue backlog; this increases end-to-end p95/p99 even though GPU decode time unchanged.
- Autoscaling events show no additional workers were added during the spike; scaling cooldown was hit because of transient CPU pressure on the control plane (k8s scheduler flapping on a noisy node pool).
- Error rate (5xx) correlates with request timeouts when batch queues exceeded 16k (timeouts triggered by proxy at 5s).

Hypothesis: a combination of control-plane flapping + a recent batching-policy tweak allowed larger maximum batch_wait to be used (was set higher in the last config rollout). That meant when the queue length briefly spiked, our runtime favored waiting to build larger batches, increasing latency for all queued requests.

I'm attaching a small dump of representative requests. Next steps: 1) force smaller max_batch_wait and max_batch_size for the ClarityHealth routing shard, 2) temporarily increase worker pool to drain backlog, 3) fix noisy node detection so autoscaler doesn't hit cooldown on spurious CPU blips.

-Adit
Aditya Rao
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
Attachment: request_samples.ndjson
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-30T10:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Production: sudden p99 jumps and 5xxs this morning

Deployed mitigation at 10:12 PT:
- Reduced max_batch_wait for ClarityHealth routing shard from 250ms -> 40ms.
- Capped max_batch_size from 256 -> 64 for that shard.
- Temporarily added two hot-warm nodes (reserved) to the tenant pool to accelerate drain.

Result: queue_depth down to ~1.7k by 10:28 PT, p95 moved back toward ~360ms and p99 below ~1.2s. Error rate dropped to 0.06%. Patch diff attached (small config change).

We will follow up with a post-incident action item: revert the risky batching-policy rollout to a canary-only flag and improve autoscaler noisy-node detection.

Attachments: mitigation_patch.diff, p99_timeseries.png

-Monica

Date: 2027-01-30T15:00:00Z
Subject: Executive summary: ClarityHealth hosted API latency regression (post-mitigation)

Team / Tom / Emma —

Summary (what happened):
- 07:25–08:40 PT we observed a tenant-specific backlog on the Hosted API routing shard for ClarityHealth; queue depth peaked ~18k. Our batching policy allowed long waits to form larger batches during the spike, which amplified p95/p99 latency and triggered proxy timeouts (5s).

Impact:
- Customer-visible p95 increased from ~320ms -> ~1.4s; p99 exceeded 4s for the worst 15-minute window. Error rate peaked at ~0.9%. Affected clinician flows experienced intermittent timeouts (estimated 12 user-facing timeouts).

What we changed (mitigation):
- Immediate config change at 10:12 PT: max_batch_wait -> 40ms, max_batch_size -> 64 for ClarityHealth shard. Added temporary capacity to drain the queue.
- Backlog drained and p95/p99 returned close to baseline within ~15 minutes.

Root cause (preliminary):
- Interaction between a recent batching-policy rollout (increased max_batch_wait) and a transient noisy-node event that prevented autoscaler from adding capacity; together they caused queue accumulation and larger batching latency.

Next steps (action items):
1) Roll back the risky batching-policy rollout to canary-only and run targeted load tests (owner: Product/Runtime, ETA: 2027-02-04).
2) Improve autoscaler noisy-node detection and shorten cooldown window (owner: Infra/SRE, ETA: 2027-02-07).
3) Add tenant-level safety limits that automatically switch to low-latency batching when queue_depth > 8k (owner: Runtime, ETA: 2027-02-03).
4) Customer follow-up: formal incident summary + service credit proposal (owner: TAM, ETA: 2027-01-31).

Requested from leadership: approval to grant ClarityHealth a one-time service credit for the incident window (proposed amount: one week of hosted credits prorated to their committed usage). Please advise if finance approval / exec sign-off is required.

Relevant artifacts attached and linked.

-Grace
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
